summary: The evidence does not establish a cause for the incident. The clearest measured change is that llm-gateway tokens_per_min left its ~41k baseline at 10:55Z and pinned at 400000 from 11:00Z while request rate stayed flat, and llm-gateway and orchestrator latency rose in the same minute. The leading possibilities are an orchestrator get_holdings agent loop that started at 10:55:20Z, or inflated prompts, but the link to token cost is unverified and no per-call token data exists. Separately, msg-delivery began failing template renders for 'portfolio_value' right after the 11:24Z refactor deploy, but no blank notification was actually observed. Missing: prompt/completion split, LLM calls per session, rendered notification content, and whether portfolio_value is null upstream or missing in the template.

hypotheses.statement: The msg-delivery notification template refactor (msg-delivery-00290, 11:24Z) broke rendering so 'portfolio_value' is missing, which causes failed notifications and redeliveries on outbound-msgs, separately from the assistant slowness and token cost.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: msg-delivery deployed a notification template refactor at 11:24Z, and err_rate stepped up at 11:25Z from a ~0.005 baseline. The first render failure ('missing variable portfolio_value') came at 11:25:18Z, and no render failures were logged before the deploy.
Redeliveries on outbound-msgs began at 11:25:37Z, shortly after the first render failure, consistent with failed renders being retried.

contradicting.text: No blank notifications are observed anywhere: no WARN lines about blank bodies, and sends and receipts continue as ok/delivered. It is only an assumption that the render failures produce the blank notifications users reported.
Failed renders are redelivered, not dead-lettered (DLQ stayed at 0), so it is not shown that a failed message reaches a user with an empty body.

The timing alone supports the deploy; it is not shown that the field is missing in the template rather than null upstream in the payload. This hypothesis also cannot explain the assistant slowness or token cost.

hypotheses.statement: llm-gateway is consuming far more tokens per request than before, through inflated prompts or repeated LLM calls, because request rate stayed flat while tokens_per_min jumped at 10:55Z toward the 400000 ceiling; this slows llm-gateway and the orchestrator that calls it and fires the token-cost alert, with the trigger not yet identified.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: Request rate stayed flat while tokens_per_min jumped at 10:55Z (about 41.6k to 101.9k) and then ramped to the 400000 value, so the growth is not explained by more traffic. It is likely that it comes from larger requests per call, though this is an assumption.

contradicting.text: No prompt, completion or LLM-call-count data exists to confirm inflation or repeated calls; the log queries returned nothing and no such metrics are available.
No llm-gateway change is recorded in the window, so no trigger has been identified.
Fallback and parse-failure rates were flat, which does not support a parse-failure driver.

hypotheses.statement: The upstream LLM provider is degraded, which slows llm-gateway and orchestrator independently of token growth, possibly with client retries inflating tokens.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: llm-gateway provider-latency warnings were present from the start of the window, so some provider-side slowness is logged.

contradicting.text: Provider-latency warnings were less frequent after 10:55Z (about 0.09/min) than before (about 0.16/min), so they do not track the step change.
No retry or timeout lines appear in llm-gateway logs, so there is no sign of client retries inflating tokens. The warnings are threshold-based and sampled, so this does not rule the hypothesis out.

hypotheses.statement: An orchestrator agent loop (repeated get_holdings tool calls, x38 per aborted session) starting at 10:55:20Z multiplies LLM calls per user request, which inflates tokens through llm-gateway at flat rps, slows llm-gateway and orchestrator, and produces the llm-gateway upstream timeouts that follow at 10:58Z.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: Orchestrator agent-loop aborts (get_holdings x38 per session) begin at 10:55:20Z, in the same minute as the token and latency jump, at 3 per minute through 11:19Z.
The first orchestrator upstream timeouts on llm-gateway come at 10:58:17Z, after the loop onset.
Request rate stayed flat while tokens rose, which is consistent with more LLM calls per user request; the proposed link is an assumption.

contradicting.text: No orchestrator change is recorded, so there is no identified trigger for the loop.
portfolio-svc request rate shows no step at 10:55Z, so no extra downstream call volume is visible. The loop's call volume would be small relative to the band, so this is not conclusive.
The llm_calls log query returned nothing, so LLM calls per session were not measured. A constant 3 aborts per minute also does not by itself explain the steep ramp and cap in tokens.

facts.text: llm-gateway fallback_pct and parse_fail_pct are constant across the window, which weakens a parse-failure explanation for the latency rise.
Provider latency warnings began at the start of the window, before the token alerts, and continued intermittently.
msg-delivery returned no WARN lines containing 'body' in the window, so no blank-body warnings were logged there.
msg-delivery deployed a notification template refactor about 16 minutes before the incident report, the only deploy near onset in the window that touches notifications.
llm-gateway tokens_per_min leaves its baseline (about 40k to 44k per minute from 10:00 to 10:54Z) in the 10:55Z minute, jumping to 101905.063.
msg-delivery err_rate stepped up at the 11:25Z point, one minute after the 11:24Z deploy, from a baseline near 0.004.
outbound-msgs dead-letter queue stayed at 0 for the whole window, so failed renders were redelivered rather than dead-lettered.
llm-gateway has no recorded deploy, config, migration or flag change between 09:00 and 11:30Z on 2026-03-27; the result was complete.
orchestrator has no recorded deploy, config, migration or flag change between 09:00 and 11:30Z on 2026-03-27; the result was complete.
The llm-gateway log query for prompt_tokens returned no lines in 10:00Z to 11:30Z, with no truncation or partial flag.
The orchestrator log query for llm_calls returned no lines in 10:00Z to 11:30Z, with no truncation or partial flag.
Loop-abort lines run at 3 per minute from 10:55 to 11:19Z (25 minutes), with 75 total and none before 10:55Z. The last one is at 11:19:58Z.
The first llm-gateway upstream timeout logged by orchestrator is at 10:58:17Z, about three minutes after the loop-abort onset.
portfolio-svc rps does not step at 10:55Z: 44.76 at 10:54Z, then 45.452 at 10:55Z. Call volume does not visibly rise at the loop onset.
msg-delivery's first render failure in the 11:00-11:24:59Z span is absent: a WARN-or-higher search for 'render' over 11:00-11:24:59Z returned no lines, and the first failure appears at 11:25:18Z.
The first template render failure after the 11:24Z deploy is for missing variable 'portfolio_value'.
Successful WhatsApp sends continue during the render-failure period, which argues against a complete send outage.
Redeliveries on outbound-msgs begin at 11:25:37Z, after the first render failure.

After 10:55Z there were 3 provider-latency WARNs (10:56:16, 11:02:00, 11:21:07), about 0.09 per minute over 35 minutes, so the rate is lower after the step, not higher. Counted from the returned lines.
The 'retry' search over all llm-gateway log levels in 10:00-11:30Z returned no lines, so there is no logged retry activity from this service in the window.
The 'timeout' search over all llm-gateway log levels in 10:00-11:30Z returned no lines, so llm-gateway logs contain no timeout lines in the window.
llm-gateway request rate (rps) did not rise during the token jump. It was 68.548 at 10:55Z and 70.034 at 11:00Z.
The first orchestrator agent-loop abort in the 10:50-11:20Z window (no level filter) is at 10:55:20Z; each line reports get_holdings repeated x38 in one session.

assumptions.text: The msg-delivery template refactor is a plausible cause of the blank notifications, but nothing in the data shows the rendered output changed.

Flat portfolio-svc rps does not exclude the loop. Three aborted sessions per minute at about 38 get_holdings calls each would be about 114 calls/min, roughly 1.9 rps, which sits inside the 42-48 rps band. Redis hit ratio (E-021) may also absorb repeated reads. The log lines count sessions, not calls, and portfolio-svc does not split by endpoint, so this is unverified.

The portfolio_value render failures are the likely cause of the notification problem, and the 11:24Z template refactor is a plausible trigger, because the err_rate step and first render failure both follow the deploy within about a minute. Neither is confirmed: the logs show render failures, not what was sent to users.

Blank notifications are not evidenced by these logs. A render failure may mean the message is not sent or is redelivered, and the logs do not show whether any failed message reached a user with an empty body.

Because provider-latency WARNs are sparse and steady-to-lower after 10:55Z, and no retry or timeout lines appear in llm-gateway logs, the data does not support a provider slowdown with client retries as the driver of the 10:55Z token rise. This does not rule it out, because the WARN is threshold-based and sampled.

Since request rate stayed flat while tokens rose about 16x in the first minutes, the growth is more likely to come from larger requests per call than from more calls. Prompt or completion size cannot be confirmed from these metrics.

Loop onset (10:55:20Z) falls in the same 10:55 minute bucket as the token jump (E-047/E-082) and precedes the first token-threshold WARN at 10:55:52Z (E-054). That ordering fits loops starting at 10:55Z, but 1-minute metric resolution cannot establish whether loops led the token rise. Not verified.

unresolved critic challenge C7: The loop-abort rate is flat at 3 per minute (E-093), but tokens_per_min rises from 41k to 102k to 340k to 400k over 10:55-11:00Z and then pins. A constant abort rate does not explain a ramp or a clamp. The aborts are also the sessions that were stopped, so they may be a symptom of a broader loop or context-bloat problem rather than the source of the extra tokens. portfolio-svc rps and latency show no step at 10:55Z (E-098, E-100). If the loops were driving the token cost, a rise in call volume would be expected somewhere downstream.

unresolved critic challenge C8: Blank notifications are not observed anywhere. Sends and receipts continue as 'ok' and 'delivered' (E-109, E-110). The DLQ is 0 and failed renders are redelivered (E-068), and the 'portfolio_value' error could come from an upstream null field rather than from the 11:24Z template refactor. H2 therefore has timing support only, and there is no check that the field is missing in the payload rather than in the template.

No logs were queried for wa-webhook, orchestrator or llm-gateway, so I cannot confirm their error causes. Their err_rate summaries are all low (0.001–0.008) despite high orchestrator/llm-gateway latency.
